items.title: Robotics needs better CAD, so I wrote a B-rep kernel and 3,487 tests
items.description: Hey HN, I’m Tony. I’m a co-founder of Springcraft, where we have been doing a lot of CAD modeling for robot parts.
items.ai_summary: An open-source boundary-representation geometry kernel written in safe Rust provides exact measurement, booleans, fillets, sweeps, and STEP support for CAD modeling.

items.title: Private certificate authority support in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity
items.description: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports private certificate authorities (CAs), so your agents can connect to self-hosted identity providers that use a private CA.
items.ai_summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity update that adds private certificate authority support so agents can connect to self-hosted identity providers.

items.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation
items.description: UltraTex employs a cascaded multi-view framework that integrates physical knowledge and vision-language model features to accurately generate physically plausible PBR texture maps.

items.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling
items.description: We introduce $Z$-sight, a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action (VLA) and generative latent world modeling.
items.ai_summary: Z-sight is a unified robot foundation model that couples vision-language-action modeling with generative latent world modeling to improve robotic control.

items.title: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
items.description: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier.
items.ai_summary: Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference is a contrastive prototype method for detecting large language model jailbreaks using only binary safety labels.

items.title: Knowing What You Know: A Trait Theory of Reviewer Value in Human-AI Cognitive Systems
items.description: When a capable model and a human reviewer cooperate on the same decision, which human still adds value?
items.ai_summary: A trait theory of reviewer value in human-AI cognitive systems that demonstrates metacognitive calibration governs review quality rather than speed or tenure.

items.title: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
items.description: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented.
items.ai_summary: A pipeline and large-scale dataset for mapping organizations, dependencies, vulnerabilities, and market concentration within the artificial intelligence supply chain.

items.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
items.description: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation.
items.ai_summary: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta is a requirement-centered loop that aligns agent harness evolution with real-world user requirements to improve task performance.

items.title: Unified Law for Visual Tasks (The Four Laws of Computer Vision)
items.description: A unified framework, World Snapshot Models, is proposed to train and perform nearly all visual tasks by reformulating them as generation tasks, validated across over 1,000 visual tasks.
items.ai_summary: Unified Law for Visual Tasks proposes four principles to enable a single framework to uniformly train and perform nearly all computer vision tasks.

items.title: PrismRestore: A Compact Restoration Toolbox for Agentic Image Restoration
items.description: Agentic image restoration composes operations to handle mixed degradations, yet its toolbox often requires storing multiple restoration networks. We propose PrismRestore, which constructs a compact bank of callable restoration actions from a single frozen all-in-one model.
items.ai_summary: PrismRestore is a compact image restoration toolbox that constructs callable restoration actions from a single frozen model using task-dependent channel modulation.

items.title: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
items.description: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization.
items.ai_summary: A mathematical study of stochastic gradient descent dynamics in two-layer neural networks that explains how parameter variance outside the teacher subspace harms generalization.

items.title: ShadowTransfer: A Geographic Transfer Benchmark for Overhead Shadow Detection
items.description: Overhead aerial imagery feeds dense-prediction pipelines that are routinely trained in one geographic region and deployed in another, yet no benchmark measures how shadow detection models transfer across regions.
items.ai_summary: ShadowTransfer is a geographic transfer benchmark for overhead shadow detection that introduces a plug-in module called Spectral Information Bottleneck to improve model adaptation across different cities.

items.title: Equivariant Modeling with Polynomial Features via Minimal Homogeneous Generators
items.description: We present a general framework for modeling and learning equivariant functions between finite dimensional semisimple real group representations, unifying constructions developed across many application areas.
items.ai_summary: A Python package automatically computes minimal homogeneous generators for invariant algebras and covariant modules to fit equivariant polynomial feature models for scientific applications.

items.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents
items.description: User simulators offer a scalable way to evaluate interactive agents, but how to assess their quality remains underexplored. In particular, it is unclear whether existing user simulator evaluation frameworks reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior.
items.ai_summary: An evaluation suite for interactive agent user simulators combines utility and two fidelity measures to successfully detect ten simulated user behavior failures.

items.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity
items.description: A fixed dispatch rate for LLM inference becomes stale as serving fleets resize and request sizes change. Generative output length is unknown at admission, and shared provider pools can lose capacity.
items.ai_summary: Cap-and-Track is an asynchronous request dispatch design that uses backend refusal signals to dynamically scale LLM inference capacity without requiring output-length predictions.

items.title: Who are you? The Personal Imitation Game
items.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) now perform strongly on Alan Turing's 1950 Imitation Game, so we propose a harder challenge, the Personal Imitation Game, which asks whether a machine can replicate a specific individual in conversation rather than a generic human.
items.ai_summary: The Personal Imitation Game is a conversational challenge testing whether an AI system can replicate a specific individual using digital communication data.

items.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation
items.description: Large language models have been widely used to generate plausible research ideas, yet it remains unclear what makes automated ideation effective and how generated novel proposals arise from prior scientific work.
items.ai_summary: The Creative AI Researcher is an agentic framework that constructs semantic knowledge graphs and uses explicit conceptual operators to generate methodologically novel research ideas.

items.title: Monoculture Robust Learning
items.description: We introduce a notion of monoculture robustness in Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) learning, as a way to mitigate the problem of algorithmic monoculture (Kleinberg and Raghavan, 2021): the tendency of models sharing the same components (e.g., training data) to fail on the…
items.ai_summary: Monoculture robustness in PAC learning achieves exponentially shrinking joint failure probabilities by repeatedly running replicable base learners on a single dataset.

items.title: Local AI Agents in Power Electronics Simulation: Deployment, Measurements and Costs
items.description: Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging in power electronics, where it drives the simulation loop that engineers used to close largely by hand.
items.ai_summary: A systematic evaluation framework measures the power, energy, token, and time costs of running local AI agents on power electronics simulation tasks.

items.title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
items.description: Large language models (LLMs) are used to explain clinical prediction models, on the promise that they can say what a model computes, find its faults and even reveal new knowledge in it. We tested the three promises where the answers could be checked.
items.ai_summary: A large language model audited black-box clinical prediction models through queries alone, successfully reproducing their log-odds and identifying planted flaws.

items.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation
items.description: Large-scale, multi-agent self-play trains robust driving policies effectively in simulation, but controlling these models to generate specific, safety-critical edge cases remains a key challenge.
items.ai_summary: An extended multi-agent self-play framework conditions driving policies on agent-relative dynamic goals to generate controllable and interactive safety-critical scenarios for autonomous vehicle testing.

items.title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision
items.description: Neural PDE operators are often optimized through state reconstruction, which largely constrains operator values at observed inputs but does not fully characterize their sensitivity to local perturbations.
items.ai_summary: TangentPDE is a plug-and-play training framework that uses sparse finite-difference supervision to learn both neural operator values and their local perturbation variations.

items.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
items.description: A rule-graph-based generative world model preserves user-defined rules and world states across saving and loading while accurately realizing rule-induced visual changes on designated objects and attributes.

items.title: Choosing What to Observe: Budget-Paired Counterfactual Audits for Credible Evaluation of Visual Agents
items.description: Visual agents that read dense documents must ration a finite observation budget across candidate regions, yet answer accuracy conflates where an agent looks, how it adapts to the reads that remain, and how it an?swers once observation stops.
items.ai_summary: Budget-paired counterfactual audits are an evaluation protocol that decomposes lost expected accuracy into stepwise acquisition loss and terminal decision loss for visual agents.

items.title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
items.description: Underwater navigation requires translating visual spatial cues into motion, yet marine vision-language datasets rarely include paired robot trajectories.
items.ai_summary: NereidVLA is a vision-language-action model that transfers marine spatial knowledge to language-conditioned three-dimensional underwater navigation.

items.title: Gaspard: Expressive unified speech and gesture synthesis with continuous autoregressive flow-matching and decoupled classifier-free guidance
items.description: Human communication involves highly coordinated multimodal signals such as speech and co-speech gestures.
items.ai_summary: Gaspard is a unified speech-gesture generation model that uses continuous autoregressive flow-matching and decoupled classifier-free guidance to produce synchronous multimodal signals.

items.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
items.description: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible.
items.ai_summary: ExecJudges is a method that uses frontier large language models to convert assessment guidelines into executable programs for automated relevance labeling in retrieval evaluation.

items.title: Atomic MathReasoner: Instance-Level Composition of Atomic Reasoning Skills for Mathematical LLMs
items.description: Most existing approaches enhance mathematical reasoning in large language models (LLMs) as a monolithic capability, despite the fact that different mathematical problems require different reasoning skills.
items.ai_summary: Atomic MathReasoner is an instance-level framework that composes atomic reasoning skills using capability-specific LoRA experts and a lightweight router for mathematical large language models.

items.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading
items.description: Existing AI agents can retrieve information, call tools, run experiments, and produce multi-step outputs. Yet most are built around relatively static workflows and struggle to preserve reliable state as the environment changes.
items.ai_summary: Vibe-Trading is an agent-native framework and workspace that integrates market research, backtesting, and execution for building and evaluating financial trading agents.

items.title: General progress substitutes for specific training data in language models
items.description: Withholding training data delays but does not prevent language models from acquiring skills, and models can regain withheld capabilities with less data as they improve.
items.ai_summary: Research demonstrates that general language model progress on remaining training data substitutes for withheld skill data, reducing the amount of data needed to regain the skill later.

items.title: Measuring and Improving Transfer of Neural Surrogates for Vehicle Aerodynamics
items.description: Neural surrogates for external vehicle aerodynamics are fast alternatives to physics-based computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations.
items.ai_summary: GeoReplay is a geometry- and gradient-aligned source replay technique that improves the zero-shot transfer and fine-tuning accuracy of neural surrogates for vehicle aerodynamics.

items.title: Does the Action Matter? Probing Action-Conditioned Semantic Forecasting as a World Model for Autonomous Driving
items.description: World models are increasingly used in autonomous driving to predict how a scene evolves under the ego vehicle's actions, supporting counterfactual reasoning and model-based planning.
items.ai_summary: Research evaluating action-conditioned semantic forecasting for autonomous driving world models finds that incorrect actions significantly degrade prediction metrics while correct actions yield modest improvements.

items.title: Kaer: Security-Aware Replanning for Multi-Agent Systems
items.description: One popular architecture for multi-agent systems (MAS) relies on an orchestrator that generates an initial plan, coordinates its execution, and dynamically revises the plan based on agent feedback when tasks cannot be fully specified in advance.
items.ai_summary: Kaer is a multi-agent framework featuring security-aware replanning that shields planners from untrusted agent feedback by using abstract templates and deterministic repair operators to improve robustness against adversarial exploits.

items.title: What Survival Benchmarks Don't Tell You: Impact of Model Selection and Dataset Regimes
items.description: Despite the proliferation of survival analysis methods, current benchmarks often operate under narrow conditions: they heavily rely on the concordance index (C-index) for evaluation and model selection, and frequently either exclude deep learning (DL) methods or underrepresent…
items.ai_summary: Large-scale benchmark comparing survival analysis methods demonstrates that evaluation design and model selection criteria fundamentally dictate performance conclusions across diverse datasets.

items.title: Overlooked and Underutilized: Prototypes are the Missing Piece in Tabular XAI
items.description: Explainable AI (XAI) is frequently applied to high-stakes tabular data, yet the field relies heavily on feature attribution methods.
items.ai_summary: Paper arguing that incorporating prototypical parts into tabular explainable AI provides cohesive semantic units that reduce cognitive load and improve model transparency.

items.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
items.description: A foundation model fine-tuned from a large language model measures and predicts human behaviour and aligns simulated population responses with human statistics, improving accuracy over frontier LLMs.

items.title: Synthesizing hyperspectral Data using generative Models to train spectral Unmixing Methods for low-cost Crop Residue Cover Mapping
items.description: The spectral range of the Field Imaging Nanosatellite for Crop residue Hyperspectral Mapping (FINCH), developed by the University of Toronto Aerospace Team's Space System Division, poses significant challenges for hyperspectral unmixing to determine crop residue cover…
items.ai_summary: Framework for training hyperspectral unmixing models for crop residue mapping by decoupling interpolation and abundance estimation using conditional data generators to incorporate physical spectral priors.

items.title: LAaDT-DSS: decision support for non-experts on rooftop PV, incentive and grid simulations under Turkish tariff rules
items.description: Rooftop photovoltaics raise three questions: should a household invest, which incentive costs the state least, and does the feeder stay within limits? Those who ask are rarely modellers.
items.ai_summary: LAaDT-DSS is decision-support software that uses a simulation core and a language model to help non-experts analyze rooftop photovoltaic investments, state incentives, and grid limits under Turkish tariff rules.

items.title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models
items.description: FlashMorph2 performs on-policy layer selection and weight adaptation for hybrid attention Transformers, improving long-context benchmark scores while selecting layers efficiently across model scales.
items.ai_summary: FlashMorph2 is an on-policy layer-selection method for converting pretrained Transformers into hybrid attention models by evaluating discrete hybrid architectures end to end and jointly optimizing layer scores and model weights.

items.title: Advancing chip design with OpenAI models
items.description: Trending on Hacker News from openai.com. 199 points and 130 comments.

items.title: ReCoCo: From Patches to Compositions for Visual Representation Learning
items.description: Self-supervised learning has produced powerful visual representations, yet learning strong dense features remains challenging.
items.ai_summary: ReCoCo is a regional composition consistency approach for self-supervised visual representation learning that aligns patch-level predictions over visual prototypes across augmented views without requiring semantic groupings.

items.title: Edge-Efficient Joint RAW Image Compression and Restoration for Smart Wearable Devices
items.description: Smart wearable devices, such as augmented reality glasses, increasingly rely on cameras to understand and interact with their surroundings.
items.ai_summary: Asymmetric framework for joint RAW image compression and restoration on smart wearable devices that uses an on-device encoder and a backend decoder to optimize transmitted representations for clean image reconstruction.

items.title: Prognosis Without Prediction: The Intrinsic Geometry of Survival
items.description: Modeling systemic failure in high-dimensional environments is fundamentally limited by supervised algorithms that attempt to predict sparse, noisy or censored endpoints.
items.ai_summary: Self-Organizing Survival Manifolds is a deep learning framework that models system failure and patient trajectories as an emergent geometric property in a unified latent space without relying on explicit outcome regression.

items.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
items.description: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models.
items.ai_summary: Soft-MoQE is a hybrid quantum-classical architecture that replaces variational quantum training with input-dependent selection and combination of fixed quantum feature maps using a classical gating network.

items.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks
items.description: Neural networks with randomly initialized, fixed weights and trainable biases are universal approximators, yet the dynamics of bias-only training remain largely unexplored.
items.ai_summary: Researchers study bias-only training dynamics in ReLU networks using activation codes, showing that training reduces to a linear least-squares problem when codes remain fixed.

items.title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data
items.description: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) struggle with accurately capturing camera-object relations, especially for object orientation, camera viewpoint, and camera shots.
items.ai_summary: Ultimate3D is a large-scale 3D-grounded visual instruction dataset designed to improve multimodal large language models in recognizing camera-object relations.

items.title: The Elephant in the Question: Unified Models Picture the Concepts Behind Their Answers
items.description: Visualizing intermediate representations could help us inspect the reasoning steps underlying a model output. Unified multimodal models offer this opportunity by combining understanding and generation in one architecture.
items.ai_summary: V-lens is a method for visualizing intermediate concepts in unified multimodal models by directly accessing hidden states without training a decoder.

items.title: Training-free motion statistics match self-supervised behavior encoders
items.description: Self-supervised encoders for animal behavior are often trained on, or fed, hand-built movement features. We ask whether they beat those ingredients when compared fairly.
items.ai_summary: A training-free representation using generic per-frame measurements matches or beats specialized self-supervised animal behavior encoders across multiple benchmarks.

items.title: Isabelle Pool Server: a pooled verification service for prover training and multi-agent proving
items.description: Isabelle Pool Server (IPS), a verification service with a pool of warm headless Isabelle sessions behind an HTTP API, with session leasing and reclamation, memory-aware admission control, and a time budget on every call.
items.ai_summary: Isabelle Pool Server is a pooled verification service that manages warm headless Isabelle sessions to support prover training and multi-agent theorem proving.

items.title: Read Together, Answer Apart: How Earlier Questions Help Vision-Language Models Look
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) are often asked several questions about the same image in a single prompt (co-asking), yet existing evaluations report conflicting accuracy gains and hallucinations at the prompt level without tracking how individual answers change.
items.ai_summary: Read Together, Answer Apart is a training-free decoding mask that prevents cross-question interference in vision-language models when answering multiple questions about the same image.

items.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations
items.description: Neural networks trained on the same task develop related weight-space structures, yet remain distinguishable after learning. Do these differences merely reflect alternative solutions, or do they preserve information about individual learning histories?
items.ai_summary: Experiments demonstrate that neural network weight space and internal representations preserve decodable information about initialization, task order, and intermediate learning histories.

items.title: Reconstruction vs. Prediction Pre-Training of Discrete Video Representations for Continuous Control
items.description: Self-supervised video encoders are commonly trained to either reconstruct pixels or predict latent features, yet it remains unclear how these objectives shape representations for downstream dynamics.
items.ai_summary: Researchers analyze how reconstructive and predictive pre-training objectives shape video representation properties for continuous control, revealing key trade-offs in state fidelity and autoregressive rollout.

items.title: Counterfactual World Models: JEPAs That Reason About "What If"
items.description: World models operate in a world they cannot fully observe. When a hidden disturbance, such as a current pushing a boat, changes the outcome of an action, a counterfactual question follows: what would have happened under a different action, subject to the same disturbance?
items.ai_summary: Researchers introduce a counterfactual world model framework for joint embedding predictive architectures that predicts alternative action outcomes without requiring counterfactual training data.

items.title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
items.description: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty.
items.ai_summary: 4D-TEMPO is a differentiable physical renderer that fits atomic structures directly to 4D-STEM electron counts to recover atomic positions alongside per-atom uncertainty estimates.

items.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids
items.description: Identifying high-impact attack paths in cyber-physical power systems is critical for improving grid resilience. Existing methods typically rely on either structural topology analysis or simulation-based cascading-failure models.
items.ai_summary: Physics-grounded framework that uses large language models to identify cyber-physical attack paths in smart grids, improving alignment with cascading-failure references.

items.title: Horizontal Flow Matching for Single-Cell Spatiotemporal Dynamics
items.description: Learning the spatiotemporal dynamics of cells from spatial transcriptomics requires connecting snapshots of different cells acquired in different coordinate frames. A rotation or translation of a section can appear as cell movement and distort the inferred correspondence.
items.ai_summary: HORIZON is a transformer-based model that learns spatiotemporal single-cell dynamics up to shared rigid motion, improving the accuracy of reconstructed tissue geometry and gene expression over existing methods.

items.title: Elysium: Simulation-Free Unbalanced Schrödinger Bridges
items.description: Reconstructing cellular dynamics from snapshots is challenging because the destructive nature of single-cell measurements makes tracking the same cells over time impossible.
items.ai_summary: Elysium is a simulation-free solver for unbalanced Schrödinger bridges that jointly learns state transitions and mass changes to reconstruct cellular dynamics without simulating trajectories during training.

items.title: A$^3$Bench: Compositional Reasoning over Aggressive Interactions in Videos
items.description: Recent Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved strong performance on general video understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to reason about participant roles in aggressive interactions remains largely unexplored.
items.ai_summary: A3Bench is a benchmark for evaluating multimodal large language models on compositional reasoning over aggressive interactions, participant roles, and associations in videos.

items.title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing
items.description: Online A/B testing is the standard approach for evaluating changes to user-facing systems, such as a new recommendation or ranking policy, before deployment. While the difference-in-means estimator of a standard A/B test is unbiased, it often suffers from high variance.
items.ai_summary: Variance-optimal counterfactual policy design method that jointly optimizes action sampling and control variates to reduce variance and improve sample efficiency in online A/B testing.

items.title: datasette-arrows 0.1a0
items.description: Release: datasette-arrows 0.1a0 Datasette 1.0a43 added the ability for plugins to implement streaming export formats.
items.ai_summary: Datasette-arrows 0.1a0 is a plugin release for Datasette that implements streaming export formats.

items.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
items.description: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data.
items.ai_summary: Algorithm extension featuring rejection gates that identifies new modular data for topological quantum field theories and expands the Anyon Atlas up to 42 anyons.

items.title: Cross-Vehicle Transferability of Lateral Velocity Estimation on Production Vehicles through Input Selection and Data Augmentation
items.description: Lateral velocity is safety-critical for vehicle-dynamics control but cannot be measured with production sensors.
items.ai_summary: Neural-network estimator for lateral velocity in production vehicles that uses input selection and physics-motivated data augmentations to improve cross-vehicle transferability and zero-shot accuracy.

items.title: Sex Differences in the Detection of Parkinson's Disease from Speech
items.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease in the world, and 70\% to 75\% of PD patients suffer from speech disorders at some stage.
items.ai_summary: Study evaluating speech-based Parkinson's disease detection using machine learning, finding that models trained on one sex fail to generalize to the other.

items.title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction
items.description: Accurate matched affinities determine mutation effects, but gains in aggregate affinity prediction may transfer unevenly to average effects, ordering and local accuracy. We evaluated eleven method families using method-specific matched populations.
items.ai_summary: Controlled CoPRA method that reduces absolute-affinity error and improves mean-effect accuracy for protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction.

items.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
items.description: Jeveration repurposes a frozen vision-language model to generate coherent images and perform image-to-image and dense prediction tasks in a single forward pass with fast 512x512 generation.

items.title: Approximate Dynamic Programming with Basis Function Learning
items.description: This work presents a novel approach for approximating the value function in Markov decision processes (MDPs). Our approach is grounded in the approximate linear programming (ALP) framework, wherein basis functions (BFs) play an important role.
items.ai_summary: Bellman operator basis function learning method that approximates value functions in Markov decision processes while improving computational efficiency and convergence guarantees.

items.title: HandWorldBench: A Unified Benchmark for Hand-Centric World Models
items.description: Recent advances in world models are opening new possibilities for fine-grained embodied tasks, with hand-object interaction offering a particularly demanding setting.
items.ai_summary: HandWorldBench is a unified benchmark that evaluates hand-centric world models across six dimensions using 500 carefully selected egocentric interaction clips.

items.title: How Generative Models Generate: A Concise Guide to the Generative AI Landscape
items.description: The rapidly expanding generative AI landscape brings together methods that differ in architecture, learning objective, mathematical representation and sampling procedure.
items.ai_summary: Guide that explores generative AI models by categorizing their generation routes, learning objectives, and architectures within a conceptual framework.

items.title: Surrogate Modeling and Reduced-Order Methods in Gravitational-Wave Physics and Numerical Relativity: From Spectral Representations to Adaptive Compression
items.description: The rapid expansion of gravitational-wave astronomy and high-precision numerical relativity has created an acute computational bottleneck: direct numerical integration of the Einstein field equations and high-dimensional Bayesian parameter estimation require millions of…
items.ai_summary: Reduced-order modeling and surrogate techniques that compress high-fidelity numerical relativity solutions to accelerate gravitational-wave data analysis.

items.title: Generalization of Text Line Segmentation for HTR in Historical Documents
items.description: In this paper we investigate the generalization capability of state-of-the-art object detection models (Hi-SAM, YOLO, and RT-DETR) for the automatic segmentation of text lines in historical documents.
items.ai_summary: Object detection models for automatic text line segmentation in historical documents, achieving low character error rates across datasets with diverse visual layouts.

items.title: Multi-Band Galaxy Novel-View Synthesis with Radiative Gaussian Fields
items.description: We propose a novel view synthesis tool for galaxies based on Gaussian Splatting (GS).
items.ai_summary: GalaxyGS is a physically inspired Gaussian Splatting method that synthesizes novel views of galaxies by accounting for energy emission and light propagation.

items.title: Induction Head Origins of SLAM-ASR Speech Recognition Models
items.description: What makes a small trained map from encoder states to the embedding space of a frozen language model sufficient for competitive speech recognition?
items.ai_summary: Research demonstrating that SLAM-ASR speech recognition models rely on the induction heads of a frozen language model to map speech embeddings to transcript tokens.

items.title: DRIFT: Detachable Reasoning for Runtime-Flexible and Efficient End-to-End Driving
items.description: The integration of vision-language models (VLMs) into end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving has demonstrated strong potential by providing scene description and reasoning capabilities.
items.ai_summary: DRIFT is an end-to-end autonomous driving framework that integrates a lightweight language model with runtime-flexible planning to achieve efficient scene reasoning.

items.title: Meta-LSQ: A Closed-Form Sobolev Inner Solver for Few-Shot Meta-Learning
items.description: Gradient-based meta-learners such as model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) adapt to a new task with an inner loop of gradient descent that has to be differentiated through, and they meta-learn every network weight.
items.ai_summary: Meta-LSQ is a closed-form Sobolev inner solver for few-shot meta-learning that fits tasks using regularized least-squares over a random Fourier basis.

items.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents
items.description: Agents that do science must choose informative experiments and reason from their results, but most discovery benchmarks cannot separate that skill from recall, unstated scoring rules or shortcut policies.
items.ai_summary: Openhagen Worlds is a suite of 27 procedurally generated and calibrated environments designed to measure and train scientific discovery agents.

items.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?
items.description: Deployed world-action models (WAMs) can keep improving only if they make good use of their own experience. Existing methods supply retrieved rollouts or demonstrations to the policy as context, yet such experience often turns previously solved tasks into failures.
items.ai_summary: World-action models method called F^3 uses form, fit, and fusion to select and inject valuable past rollouts, improving policy success rates and reducing steps and regressions.

items.title: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?
items.description: Omni-modal large language models (omni-modal LLMs) can respond to spoken requests directly through voice and video calls. Such requests rely on the scene shared by the user and the assistant, so the same utterance may call for different help or for no response.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation benchmark called O-IN-Bench assesses how well omni-modal large language models understand spoken intentions and scene context during video and voice interactions.

items.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
items.description: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances.
items.ai_summary: Task-oriented network ranging framework called S-SM-NR jointly designs task graphs and transmit-listen schedules to reduce ranging cycles and improve localization accuracy.

items.title: When Does Continual Pre-Training Help? A Controlled Study of Dialectal Adaptation for Québec French
items.description: Continual pre-training (CPT) is widely used to adapt pretrained language models to dialectal and non-standard language varieties, yet it remains unclear when this additional training is necessary, what drives its benefits, and whether aggregate evaluation scores adequately…
items.ai_summary: Controlled study of continual pre-training for Quebec French language models reveals that adaptation benefits depend heavily on starting competence and corpus composition rather than data volume alone.

items.title: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent
items.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult.
items.ai_summary: Reinforcement learning approach for language model agents uses a reverse-to-forward curriculum with advantage decomposition to solve sparse-reward long-horizon tasks.

items.title: Improving Zero-shot 3D Semantic Mapping in Offroad with Geometric Priors
items.description: Semantic 3D mapping is a powerful representation that enables platform agnostic mobile robot navigation in challenging offroad conditions.
items.ai_summary: Semantic 3D mapping method improves off-road mobile robot navigation by fusing vision foundation model predictions with sphericity-elevation geometric priors.

items.title: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning
items.description: Malicious adversaries can employ gradient inversion attacks to reverse-engineer private data using the model updates of a round in Federated Learning.
items.ai_summary: Attack pipeline reverses federated learning aggregation by iteratively subtracting recovered sentences, enabling exact text recovery from client model updates.

items.title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
items.description: A new metric for automatic CAD generation evaluates models through engineering-drawing projections with a saturating penalty along curves, exposing small local errors that volume- or surface-based metrics miss and enabling use as a reinforcement learning reward or test-time…

items.title: Predicting Species Splits: A Challenging Fine-Grained Benchmark for Category Discovery
items.description: Widely used category discovery benchmarks have become increasingly saturated and often fail to reflect real-world discovery settings, making long-term evaluation of new methods difficult.
items.ai_summary: Fine-grained benchmark called PS-SPLIT uses bird taxonomic splits with subtle visual differences and geographic metadata to evaluate category discovery methods.

items.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
items.description: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability.

items.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning
items.description: CurvDelta and CurvLoRA constrain LLM updates to a low-curvature preservation space, improving retention while maintaining target adaptation across reasoning, code, and unlearning tasks.
items.ai_summary: Scalable framework called CurvDelta incorporates capability preservation constraints into model parameter updates using low-curvature space geometry to improve adaptation and unlearning tasks.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.description: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI).
items.ai_summary: Multimodal decision model family called Piccolo coevolves model capabilities and training data through recursive self-improvement and agentic data engineering to achieve high performance on decision benchmarks.

items.title: Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models
items.description: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models.
items.ai_summary: Self-supervised reinforcement learning method that improves the structure and length of medical explanations generated by small language models.

items.title: Zonotopic Analysis of Quantization Error in Neural Networks
items.description: Quantized neural networks achieve computational efficiency by reducing precision, but bounding their quantization error remains a challenge due to discrete rounding and clamping operations.
items.ai_summary: Zonotope-based abstract interpretation framework that computes rigorous quantization error bounds for quantized neural networks with improved efficiency.

items.title: Equal Steps, Unequal Curvature: Where Muon's Update Goes Wrong
items.description: Muon updates each hidden weight matrix along the polar factor of its momentum, the steepest-descent direction under the spectral norm.
items.ai_summary: Analytical method that diagnoses curvature-related over-stepping in Muon weight updates and improves language model training loss.

items.title: AggCLIP: Aggregating CLIP for Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection
items.description: Zero-Shot Multimodal Anomaly Detection (ZSMAD) aims to identify both appearance and geometric defects in novel categories without relying on target-specific training data, making it especially valuable in real-world scenarios constrained by data scarcity, privacy concerns, or…
items.ai_summary: AggCLIP is a zero-shot multimodal anomaly detection framework that incorporates local geometric structure and spatial context to identify defects without target-specific training data.

items.title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
items.description: Multimodal language models for materials science rely on effective mechanisms for incorporating three-dimensional structural representations.
items.ai_summary: Task-Conditioned Attention Fusion is an attention-based bridge module for multimodal materials language models that dynamically combines structural representations to improve property prediction accuracy.

items.title: A Generative Model for Higher-Order Network Dynamics
items.description: Conventional network representations inferred from multivariate time series describe statistical relationships between pairs of components, even when the underlying dynamics involve group interactions that cannot be represented by pairwise interactions alone.
items.ai_summary: Generative model of stochastic network dynamics that provides controlled benchmarks featuring pairwise and directed higher-order interactions for evaluating information-theoretic measures.

items.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
items.description: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices.
items.ai_summary: Hypnos is an open-source, dual-phase edge continual learning platform that separates rapid wake-phase inference from consolidated sleep-phase training to adapt to non-stationary data streams.

items.title: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview Technical Report
items.description: We introduce Clover-35B-A3B-Preview (Clover), a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with 35 billion total parameters and 3 billion activated parameters, supporting thinking-mode generation.
items.ai_summary: Clover-35B-A3B-Preview is a mixture-of-experts diffusion language model with thinking-mode generation that achieves high performance on agent benchmarks and fast generation speeds.

items.title: H3Remover: Reinforcing Video Object Removal without Paired Data
items.description: Pretrained video editors possess rich removal and completion priors, yet may retain targets or alter unrelated content. We present H3Remover, which reinforces MiniMax-H3 Base Ref2VA for video object removal without paired object-free training targets.
items.ai_summary: H3Remover is a training method for video object removal that uses depth and appearance rewards to remove target objects while preserving background content without paired data.

items.title: Transferring an analysis of human brain organization to language models
items.description: During human cortical development, functional systems become increasingly differentiated. We asked whether improved reasoning in language models involves a comparable regional reorganization.
items.ai_summary: Diffusion-map embedding technique that identifies transferable reasoning-related weight layers in language models to improve mathematical and medical reasoning performance.

items.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Location Encoding Methods for Species Distribution Modelling
items.description: Understanding the spatial distribution of species is a key question in ecology. A variety of solutions, from statistical, traditional machine learning, through to deep learning-based methods have been proposed.
items.ai_summary: Evaluation framework that quantifies the effectiveness of different location encodings for species distribution modeling at local and global scales.

items.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits
items.description: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes important for detecting unsafe or unintended actions.
items.ai_summary: GateWatch is a compact, interpretable LLM monitoring classifier that uses Boolean logic over binarized sparse autoencoder features to detect unintended actions with low computational overhead.

items.title: EgoJev: Finding Evidence in Egocentric Video by Reading VLM Decisions
items.description: Questions about long egocentric video often depend on one brief moment, such as the second a hand puts an object down. A vision-language model (VLM) that sees a few evenly spaced frames usually misses it.
items.ai_summary: EgoJev is a training-free frame selector for wearable assistants that uses vision-language model outputs to efficiently locate specific moments in long egocentric videos.

items.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN
items.description: Characteristics of Artificial Intelligence (AI) severely restrict human control. This creates new challenges for socio-technical systems design especially in safety-critical domains, where control over risks is essential along with the accountability for any harm caused.
items.ai_summary: ALIGN is a scenario-based method designed to support AI governance and stakeholder involvement by assessing the alignment between accountability and control in high-risk use cases.

items.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery
items.description: Diffusion models have transformed generative modeling through their ability to capture and generate samples from complex data distributions.
items.ai_summary: Researchers demonstrate that diffusion models serve as provably efficient priors for solving sparse recovery problems in compressed sensing within polynomial time.

items.title: Morpho-Spectral Projection Analysis (MSPA) for Plant Spectroscopy
items.description: Plant reflectance spectroscopy across the visible, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared domain encodes foliar biochemical and anatomical traits into contiguous spectral signatures with locally differentiable structure; however, extreme inter-band collinearity and unfavorable…
items.ai_summary: Morpho-Spectral Projection Analysis is a supervised dimensionality reduction operator that compresses plant reflectance spectra while improving predictive modeling performance for biochemical traits.

items.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers
items.description: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting improves the performance of Large Language Models by eliciting intermediate reasoning steps.
items.ai_summary: A method that uses chain-of-thought hidden states to derive task-solving directions for direct prompts, improving model accuracy while using a fraction of the generation tokens.

items.title: DAL: Dynamic Angular Loss for Imbalanced Medical Image Classification
items.description: Class imbalance remains a major obstacle in medical image classification, where rare but clinically important classes are often overshadowed by majority categories.
items.ai_summary: Dynamic angular loss is a classification method combining batch-adaptive angular margins and dynamically-weighted cross entropy to improve accuracy on imbalanced medical image datasets.

items.title: From Activity Recognition to Shift Detection: Variational Wi-Fi Sensing with Evidential Uncertainty
items.description: Human motion perturbs wireless channels, making commodity Wi-Fi devices a practical platform for device-free activity recognition.
items.ai_summary: Wi-HAR is a multi-antenna Wi-Fi sensing architecture that uses variational auto-encoders for human activity recognition and evidential deep learning to detect deployment shifts.

items.title: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code
items.description: Pre-trained models can read screens and reason about games, yet on an unfamiliar game, an agent still has to learn to play.
items.ai_summary: A framework where visual game agents self-improve by writing, testing, and revising programs between attempts to act in real time during unfamiliar games.

items.title: Large Language Models or AI Agents for English to Arabic Translation? An assessment on WikiEn-Ar190
items.description: This research investigates whether a large language model or an autonomous AI Agent performs better at translating from English to Arabic, which is considered a low-resource language.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces WikiEn-Ar190 and evaluates GPT-5-mini for English-to-Arabic translation, showing that autonomous reasoning methods improve translation consistency and lexical accuracy for low-resource languages.

items.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events
items.description: Visual foundation models provide powerful representations for diverse tasks, but their features become stale as visual content changes between image observations. Refreshing them requires new frames and repeated runs of a computationally expensive image encoder.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces ALIVE, an event-based method that incrementally updates visual foundation model features between image observations to reduce computational costs and improve real-world perception performance.

items.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
items.description: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes BaseRSI, a paradigm of recursive harness internalization that allows a base vision-language model to improve its own weights through training-free edits on its responses.

items.title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
items.description: Looped language models deepen reasoning at a compact parameter count by iterating a shared layer stack T times per token, turning recurrence depth directly into sequential decoding latency.

items.title: AGAMOTTO: An AI-Enabled Framework for Time-Critical Tactical Course-of-Action Evaluation and Generation
items.description: Current command and control (C2) platforms lack integrated simulation capabilities that would allow commanders to dynamically explore courses of action (COAs) during live operations.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents the ongoing development of AGAMOTTO, an AI-enabled framework designed to support time-critical tactical decision-making and course-of-action generation during military operations.

items.title: Objective-Specialized Residual Streams in Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
items.description: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extend a Transformer's residual stream into multiple parallel streams with learned cross-stream connections. Prior work trains all streams toward a shared objective.
items.ai_summary: This study investigates objective-specialized residual streams in manifold-constrained hyper-connections, demonstrating that assigning distinct learning objectives to parallel streams improves task performance through specialized read and write routing.

items.title: Beyond Appearance: Evidence-Guided Programmatic 3D Scene Reconstruction with Agentic Lighting Reasoning
items.description: Image-to-code methods for 3D scene reconstruction produce executable code that generates editable digital content and supports visual simulation.
items.ai_summary: This paper presents LightHarness, a vision-language model agentic framework that incorporates explicit lighting reasoning and memory into iterative 3D scene reconstruction from images.

items.title: Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime
items.description: In this paper, we study stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime, where the population objective shares a common minimizer with the sample losses.
items.ai_summary: This paper derives high-probability convergence guarantees and moment-based bounds for stochastic gradient descent in the smooth interpolation regime across various step-size schedules.

items.title: SCR: Detecting Backdoor-Poisoned Samples through Clean-Reference Residuals
items.description: Deep neural networks are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, in which adversaries manipulate model predictions by injecting poisoned samples into training data.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes Semantic Counterfactual Residualization, a method that uses clean reference samples to detect backdoor-poisoned training data by identifying coherent feature deviations from clean baselines.

items.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
items.description: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes.
items.ai_summary: This paper introduces a method for visualizing and measuring artificial neural network decision boundary geometry directly in high-dimensional input space to analyze curvatures, distances, and training impacts.

items.title: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning
items.description: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence.
items.ai_summary: This paper proposes NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for multimodal knowledge graph reasoning that jointly optimizes retrieval-free and retrieval-aware views through instruction tuning and structure-constrained decoding.

items.title: Fuse Before Reconstruct: A Novel Reconstruction Paradigm for Multimodal Industrial Anomaly Detection
items.description: Industrial anomaly detection plays a pivotal role in precision manufacturing, where joint analysis of multimodal data emerges as a critical approach to enhance detection accuracy.
items.ai_summary: Feature reconstruction paradigm called Fuse Before Reconstruct that fuses multimodal features before reconstruction to improve industrial anomaly detection accuracy.

items.title: Do Frontier Model Ingredients Add Up? A Replicated Factorial Study of Small Language Models
items.description: Building a small language model requires choosing which published improvements to combine. We compare five changes in the same model, using the same data and training budget. We test selected combinations and repeat each one with a second random seed.
items.ai_summary: Study comparing small language model improvements finding that mixture-of-experts layers, Muon optimization, and Gated DeltaNet hybrids yield the largest performance gains.

items.title: ProbMedTOD: A Bayesian Network Guided Task-Oriented Dialogue System for Patient History Taking
items.description: Patient history taking is a strategic, multi-turn process that refines diagnostic hypotheses through iterative questioning, mirroring clinical reasoning where each inquiry updates beliefs over candidate diagnoses.
items.ai_summary: Task-oriented dialogue system named ProbMedTOD that uses automatically synthesized clinical Bayesian networks to enable probabilistic reasoning for patient history taking.

items.title: SCRiD: Spatial and Contextual References for Generalizable AI-Generated Video Detection
items.description: Generalizable AI-generated video detection remains challenging because natural motion and content variations can resemble synthesis artifacts, making isolated video discrepancies unreliable indicators of authenticity.
items.ai_summary: Spatial and Contextual Reference-informed Detection framework that uses matched-coordinate residual responses and content-conditioned denoising references to generalize AI-generated video detection.

items.title: MECI: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction for Multimodal Entity Linking
items.description: Multimodal Entity Linking (MEL) aims to disambiguate mentions in multimodal contexts by grounding them to specific entities in a knowledge base.
items.ai_summary: Multi-Element Collaborative Interaction framework that uses a multi-view experts network and hierarchical interactions to improve multimodal entity linking.

items.title: RAID: Representation Autoencoder for Intrinsic Decomposition
items.description: Single-image intrinsic decomposition is an inherently ill-posed problem, requiring the disentanglement of strongly coupled appearance factors from a single RGB observation.
items.ai_summary: Representation Autoencoder for Intrinsic Decomposition model that uses DINOv3 features to predict intrinsic properties in a structured latent space 100 times faster than diffusion-based methods.

items.title: ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation
items.description: LLM-based artificial societies exhibit rich behavior but often lack scientific grounding: personas and environments are assumed, interaction networks are synthetic, and simulators are generated as free-form code, making results difficult to tie to real populations and sensitive…
items.ai_summary: Zero-code agent called ABSClaw that compiles natural-language requests into executable social simulations grounded in real-world census, geospatial, and survey data.

items.title: Comparing Each Generation with Independent Siblings Gives Video World Model Post-Training a Proper Objective for Outcome Frequencies
items.description: Video world models are used as simulators, so when a first frame leaves several physical outcomes open, repeated generations should produce each outcome as often as it occurs in the data.
items.ai_summary: Sibling-paired Policy Optimization method that uses independent generation siblings to weight video world model post-training outcomes according to their data frequencies.

items.title: Sparse designs via quantization of the uniform measure on high-dimensional hypercubes
items.description: While the notions of sphere packing and sphere covering underlie the most widely used criteria for space-filling design in computer experiments, namely, the maximin and minimax approaches, they suffer from major drawbacks in high dimensions.
items.ai_summary: Method for generating random designs in high-dimensional hypercubes by minimizing the quantization error of the uniform measure to avoid boundary sensitivities.

items.title: The Largest Tractable Subclass of Multi-Scale Allen Temporal Reasoning
items.description: In this paper, we propose a novel model for temporal reasoning over multi-scale intervals. We show that this model yields a complete reasoning framework and exhibits other particularly interesting properties.
items.ai_summary: New temporal reasoning model and its maximal tractable subalgebra for reasoning over multi-scale intervals in qualitative scales contexts.

items.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning
items.description: GPUs are expensive, yet latency-critical large language model (LLM) inference leaves part of them idle. Colocation reclaims this capacity by running best-effort work, such as fine-tuning, alongside serving.
items.ai_summary: BubbleTea is a colocation system that leverages expert-parallel idle time in mixture-of-experts language models to run fine-tuning tasks 1.9 to 6.2 times faster than existing methods.

items.title: RECLAIM: Robot-Vision-Informed Adversarial Patch Defense via Embodied Attention Feedback
items.description: Vision-language-action policies control embodied agents through a perception-action loop grounded in physical interaction, where adversarial patches can corrupt action predictions and thereby alter subsequent observations.
items.ai_summary: RECLAIM is an inference-time defense method that uses frozen vision-language-action model attention responses and robot geometry to protect embodied agents against adversarial visual patches.

items.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits
items.description: Frontier coding agents increasingly exhibit overeagerness, taking surprising, sometimes reckless actions beyond a user's mandate --- reported in recent system cards from frontier model developers.
items.ai_summary: Continuation audits are a pipeline that uses real coding-agent transcripts to evaluate overeagerness and unsafe behaviors in frontier AI models without triggering synthetic-setup awareness.

items.title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
items.description: Function-level vulnerability detectors often exhibit fix reversal, assigning a higher vulnerability probability to a fixed version than to its vulnerable counterpart. Fixes usually lengthen functions, and larger length increases are associated with more severe reversal.
items.ai_summary: CFVul is a function-level vulnerability detection method that uses content and length constraints to reduce fix reversal errors across multiple pretrained code models.

items.title: Study and Improvement of Search Algorithms in Stochastic Perfect-Information
items.description: In this article, we generalize Unbounded Minimax, the state- of-the-art search algorithm for deterministic zero-sum two- player games with perfect information to the framework of stochastic zero-sum two-player games with perfect informa- tion.
items.ai_summary: Generalized unbounded minimax is a new search algorithm that improves performance over existing stochastic search methods in stochastic zero-sum two-player games with perfect information.

items.title: Latent Action Policies from Suboptimal Data
items.description: Latent Action Models (LAMs) learn control representations from action-free video, but existing pipelines typically train latent policies with behavioral cloning, without an explicit policy improvement objective.
items.ai_summary: LAPIS is a goal-conditioned latent policy improvement method that uses observed state-latent transitions and a conditional flow policy to learn effective latent action models from suboptimal and action-free data.

items.title: Every Query Routes Itself: Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers with Per-Query Routed Sparse Attention
items.description: Self-attention over long token sequences dominates the inference cost of video diffusion transformers. Clustering-based sparse attention clusters both queries and keys and lets all queries in a cluster share one selection of key clusters.
items.ai_summary: Per-Query Routed Sparse Attention is a training-free method that accelerates video diffusion transformers by clustering keys and letting each query select its own key clusters independently.

items.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams
items.description: Recent research suggests that individual neurons can have interpretable roles in AI behaviour.
items.ai_summary: Steering a specific single neuron in the Qwen3.5-4B model increases information concealment behaviors in multi-agent AI teams across multiple testing scenarios.

items.title: ICICLE: In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation
items.description: Freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization allocates training budget by predicting how partially observed learning curves will continue.
items.ai_summary: ICICLE is an in-context surrogate model for learning-curve extrapolation that uses a shared set encoder to predict learning curve continuations across variable numbers of hyperparameters.

items.title: Cooperative UAV and Ground Station for Robust MEC of Dynamic Aquatic IoT: A Generative AI-Enhanced Approach
items.description: The increasing aquatic Internet of Things (AIoTs) require computational support and coverage in applications such as maritime search and rescue.
items.ai_summary: GAI-HAPPO is a generative AI-enhanced multi-agent reinforcement learning algorithm that minimizes execution time for cooperative UAV and ground station multi-access edge computing in aquatic IoT networks.

items.title: Anchoring with Visual Evidence: Explicit Semantic Anchors for Joint Change Detection and Captioning
items.description: Joint change detection and captioning seeks to localize changes and describe them from bi-temporal remote sensing images. A key challenge is translating dense visual evidence into the semantic conditions that guide description generation.
items.ai_summary: Explicit Semantic Anchors is a supervised interface for remote sensing change detection and captioning that uses visual attributes to guide text generation.

items.title: ShoWorld: Shape-Faithful Multi-Hypothesis Occupancy World Model
items.description: Occupancy world models struggle to forecast moving objects due to motion uncertainty and shape distortion. A single trajectory can average plausible futures into an implausible path, and repeated re-voxelization can erode or inflate object shape even under correct motion.
items.ai_summary: ShoWorld is a shape-faithful occupancy world model that separates motion and shape representations to forecast moving objects without shape distortion.

items.title: Harmonic Circuit: Chord Progression Lies in a Sparse Principal Information Flow in Symbolic Music Models
items.description: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) seeks to decode neural network computations into human-understandable logic. A core methodology in MI is circuit discovery: identifying the information flow in sub-networks that drive specific model behaviors.
items.ai_summary: Harmonic Circuit is a mechanistic interpretability method that identifies sparse sub-networks driving harmonic progression in symbolic music generative models.

items.title: EviScope: Evidence-Conditioned Sampling for Long-Range 3D Detection
items.description: Query-based camera-radar detectors choose where and over which frames each object query samples from the query's position or feature.
items.ai_summary: EviScope is a query-based camera-radar detection module that uses bird's-eye radar evidence to scale spatial sampling and weight multi-frame features.

items.title: Retroactive Concept Bottleneck Models for Exemplar-Free Class-Incremental Learning
items.description: Exemplar-free class-incremental learning (EFCIL) requires models to learn new classes sequentially without retaining training samples from previous tasks.
items.ai_summary: RetroCBM is an exemplar-free class-incremental learning method that uses stored statistics to supervise new visual concepts without retaining past training samples.

items.title: NativeSeg: Native Vision Language Segmentation of 3D Computed Tomography via Spatial Visual Tokens and Verified Local Zoom
items.description: Text prompted 3D computed tomography (CT) segmentation requires both full slice context and fine boundary precision across volumes where over $80\%$ of organ prompted slices lack the queried target.
items.ai_summary: NativeSeg is a native vision-language segmentation framework for 3D computed tomography that performs dense mask decoding and spatial reasoning directly over 2D visual tokens.

items.title: Explainable and CPU-Efficient Brain Tumor Classification from MRI Using Two-Phase EfficientNetB3 Fine-Tuning
items.description: Brain tumors are among the most lethal neurological disorders, with over 308,000 new diagnoses annually worldwide.
items.ai_summary: An automated deep learning pipeline uses a two-phase fine-tuned EfficientNetB3 model to classify brain tumors from MRI scans with high CPU efficiency and interpretability.

items.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training
items.description: Synthetic polysomnography (PSG) data has great potential in healthcare applications, for example in substituting real data that is sensitive and challenging to collect.
items.ai_summary: PSG-GAN is a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes multi-signal polysomnography data to train sleep apnea and sleep staging algorithms.

items.title: MLIE-CoT: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning via Multi-Level Image Editing
items.description: Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning has proven effective in improving the reasoning abilities of large language models by breaking complex tasks into step-by-step solutions.
items.ai_summary: MLIE-CoT is a visual chain-of-thought framework that uses multi-level image editing to preserve correct visual semantics and repair errors during generation.

items.title: Let a Small Model Read First: Faster Prefill for Long Interleaved Image-Text Inputs
items.description: Vision-language models (VLMs) can answer questions about long interleaved inputs, such as documents of many pages and collections of hundreds of images, but they are slow to start: on inputs of about 100K tokens, the prefill takes most of the wait for the first output token.
items.ai_summary: SkimPrefill is a fast prefill method for vision-language models that uses a small hybrid model to rank and select important input units before processing.

items.title: Keeping Shielded Data-Driven Controllers Safe Under System Evolution via Model Consistency
items.description: Cyber-physical systems (CPS) increasingly contain data-driven controllers, which raise safety concerns given their black-box nature.
items.ai_summary: Model-driven approach that integrates data-driven controllers and safety shields into a virtual underlying model, which uses consistency checking and automatic updates to maintain safety guarantees during system evolution.

items.title: DyNA-Mixer: Decoupling Time and Topology for Scalable Dynamic Node Affinity Prediction
items.description: Continuous-time dynamic graphs preserve the ordering, timing, and evolving strength of interactions that static snapshots discard, making dynamic graph mining essential for evolving systems such as recommender systems, trade networks, and transaction platforms.
items.ai_summary: DyNA-Mixer is a dynamic node affinity prediction method that decouples temporal forecasting from collaborative structure modeling to efficiently forecast continuous interaction targets and rankings in dynamic graphs.

items.title: Predicting Process-Level Behavior: A Benchmarking Study
items.description: Predictive process monitoring (PPM) typically forecasts the future of individual process instances, hence operating on trace level. Process managers, however, typically operate on process level, e.g., when assigning staff or calculating KPIs.
items.ai_summary: Benchmarking study evaluates modeling paradigms for process-level prediction tasks and finds that aggregated trace-level predictions cause compounded errors, establishing process-level prediction as a distinct predictive task.

items.title: Probing Physics in Motion Diffusion Models Against Their Own Estimate
items.description: Recent studies report that video diffusion models "know more than they show": physical properties decode better from their activations than from their inputs or outputs.
items.ai_summary: Method for probing physical knowledge in text-to-motion diffusion models finds that intermediate layers generally match the physical accuracy of the model's own clean-sample estimates, with exceptions in jump fall rates.

items.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception
items.description: LLM-based agents accumulate extensive interaction histories when solving complex, long-horizon tasks, making efficient memory management critical to their performance and scalability.
items.ai_summary: Resolution as Attention is a memory perception mechanism that dynamically adjusts the visual resolution of past interactions to reduce token consumption for LLM-based agents while preserving decision consistency.

items.title: PhysResponse: Probing the Physics of Video Generation with Controlled Interventions
items.description: Video generation models are increasingly viewed as world simulators, which requires not only plausible motion but dynamics that respond correctly to specified physical parameters.
items.ai_summary: PhysResponse is a benchmark for measuring physical parameter responsiveness in video generation models through scene-conditioned simulator inversion and event evaluation, supported by a dataset of simulated videos for fine-tuning.
